item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
896
ABPZ20 KNHC 151730
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Thu Oct 15 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Simon, located a few hundred miles south-southeast of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula, and on Hurricane
Trudy, located several hundred miles south-southwest of Acapulco,
Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form offshore of southern
Mexico during the early to middle part of next week. Environmental
conditions appear conducive for gradual development thereafter, and
a tropical depression could form during the second half of next week
while the system moves generally westward to west-northwestward over
the east to central portion of the East Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

$$
Forecaster Papin

item.description:
Issued at 1200 PM CST Thu Oct 15 2026 
689

BULLETIN
Hurricane Trudy Intermediate Advisory Number 9A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
1200 PM CST Thu Oct 15 2026
 
...HURRICANE HUNTER AIRCRAFT INVESTIGATING TRUDY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1200 PM CST...1800 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...13.4N 101.6W
ABOUT 265 MI...430 KM SSW OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 425 MI...685 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...90 MPH...150 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 345 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...979 MB...28.91 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:

None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Punta San Telmo southward to Zihuatanejo, Mexico.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere in southwestern and west-central Mexico should
continue monitor the progress of Trudy. Additional watches will
likely be required later today for portions of these areas.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1200 PM CST (1800 UTC), the center of Hurricane Trudy was located 
by Air Force Reserve Hurricane Hunter aircraft near latitude    
13.4 North, longitude 101.6 West. Trudy is moving toward the 
north-northwest near 6 mph (9 km/h). A continued motion toward the 
north-northwest is expected during the next day or so, followed by a 
turn toward the northwest this weekend. On the forecast track, Trudy 
is expected to approach the coast of southwestern and west-central 
Mexico this weekend.
 
Reports from an Air Force Reserve Hurricane Hunter aircraft 
indicate that maximum sustained winds are near 90 mph (150 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Rapid intensification is forecast over the next
day or so, and Trudy is forecast to become a major hurricane by
Friday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 25 miles (35 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105
miles (165 km).
 
The minimum central pressure estimated from the Hurricane Hunter 
aircraft data is 979 mb (28.91 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Trudy can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP1 and WMO header WTPZ41 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?key_messages.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are possible within the watch area
by early Saturday.
 
RAINFALL: Through the weekend, Trudy is expected to produce 4 to 8
inches with isolated higher totals around 12 inches through the
weekend across Colima and Jalisco. This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas along
steep terrain.
 
Elsewhere, Trudy’s outer bands are expected to produce 2 to 4 inch
with isolated higher totals around 6 inches along the southwest
Mexican coast between Guerrero and Michoacán. This rainfall may
result in localized flash flooding through the weekend, especially
in areas along steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Trudy,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Trudy are expected to begin affecting
portions of the coast of southwestern Mexico over the next day or so
and continue through the weekend. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 9
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Thu Oct 15 2026 
651 
WTPZ41 KNHC 151458
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Trudy Discussion Number   9
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
900 AM CST Thu Oct 15 2026
 
Trudy appears to be undergoing a period of rapid intensification.
After the previous advisory, there were several microwave images
that showed the hurricane has developed an eyewall, with a cyan ring
noted on the 37 GHz channel of the 1037 UTC GMI and more recent 1250
UTC WSF-M pass. This signature is often a harbinger or indicates
that rapid intensification is underway. On geostationary satellite
Trudy has been maintaining a healthy central dense overcast with
cold cloud tops between -75 to -80 C with new bursts of convection
fully wrapping around the circulation as it becomes more symmetric.
The subjective Dvorak estimate at 12 UTC was T4.5/77 kt, but given
the improving structure seen on microwave imagery, the initial
intensity is being set at 80 kt this advisory, which is on the high
end of the intensity estimates. This indicates that Trudy has
intensified 30 kt in the past 24 h, qualifying as rapid
intensification. An Air Force Reserve Hurricane Hunter aircraft is
en route to sample the hurricane and should provide critial in-situ
data to help refine the forecast this afternoon.
 
Trudy is now estimated to be moving slowly north-northwestward, or
335 degrees at 5 kt. Over the next 24-36 h Trudy is expected to
maintain this heading but at a slow pace as its steering is
maintained by two ridges, one to its east and another to its north.
These features are split by a mid- to upper-level trough that is
draped across the Yucatan Peninsula, weakening the overall
steering flow. How these synoptic features interact over the next
several days is leading to a lot of track uncertainty over the next
few days, and there are some track solutions (GFS, ECMWF) that show
Trudy making landfall. The latest NHC track forecast has been
shifted eastward compared to the prior one, following the trends in
the guidance. This track is blending the latest HFIP Corrected
Consensus Approach (HCCA), Google DeepMind ensemble mean (GDMI) and
also places a little weight on the latest ECMWF track forecast.
With that said, given the spread of the deterministic and ensemble
track guidance this cycle, this forecast is lower confidence than
usual.
 
Now that Trudy has developed an inner-core, intensification is
likely to be rapid in the short-term. Environmental conditions are
quite favorable (shear under 10 kt, sea-surface temperatures 28-29
C, and abundant moisture) and SHIPS-RI indices are elevated for a
30-40 kt increase in intensity over the next 24 h. Thus, the first
part of this intensity forecast was raised from the previous
advisory, showing Trudy becoming a major hurricane in 12-24 h, and
peaking as a 125 kt Category 4 hurricane in 36 h. This part of the
intensity forecast is on the upper end of the guidance. Thereafter,
both the GFS and ECMWF based SHIPS guidance shows southwesterly
vertical wind shear increasing markedly, and this will also be the
period where Trudy nears the coast of Mexico, where terrain-induced
effects will likely start to affect the circulation. These combined
effects are now forecast to lead to weakening beginning in 48 h and
continuing through the rest of the forecast. One big caveat with
this intensity forecast is just how close Trudy gets to Mexico. A
track closer to the coast may result in much more weakening than
shown here, while a track further offshore may preserve Trudy's
intensity, similar to what we saw with Simon earlier this week. The
second part of the NHC intensity forecast falls back closer to the
guidance mean. Given the proximity of Trudy's track to Mexico, this
is also a lower confidence intensity forecast after the next 48 h.
 
 
KEY MESSAGES:
 
1. Trudy is forecast to be a major hurricane as it approaches the
coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico this weekend. There is
an increasing risk of wind, rain, and storm surge impacts. A
Tropical Storm Watch has now been issued for a portion of the
southwestern Mexican coast, and additional watches will likely be
required further up the coast later today.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Trudy will impact the southwest
Mexican coast between Guerrero and Jalisco through the weekend. This
rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides by the
weekend across Colima and Jalisco, especially in areas along steep
terrain.
 
3. Large swells will begin to affect portions of the coast of
southwestern Mexico Friday and continue through the weekend. These
swells could cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  15/1500Z 13.1N 101.6W   80 KT  90 MPH
 12H  16/0000Z 13.6N 101.9W   95 KT 110 MPH
 24H  16/1200Z 14.6N 102.2W  115 KT 130 MPH

item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Thu Oct 15 2026 
759 
WTPZ35 KNHC 152041
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Simon Advisory Number  34
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
200 PM MST Thu Oct 15 2026
 
...SMALL SIMON SLOWLY WEAKENING AS IT DRIFTS NORTHWESTWARD...
...NOW FORECAST TO BECOME A REMNANT LOW IN A COUPLE OF DAYS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM MST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.3N 108.2W
ABOUT 270 MI...435 KM SSE OF CABO SAN LUCAS MEXICO
ABOUT 180 MI...290 KM WSW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 325 DEGREES AT 1 MPH...2 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...999 MB...29.50 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in Baja California Sur should continue to monitor Simon.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM MST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Simon was 
located near latitude 19.3 North, longitude 108.2 West. Simon is 
moving toward the northwest near 1 mph (2 km/h). A faster 
northwestward motion is forecast to begin by Friday and continue 
through the weekend.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 50 mph (85 km/h) with 
higher gusts. Gradual weakening is expected during the next few 
days, and Simon is forecast to become a post-tropical remnant low by 
this weekend.
 
Simon is a small tropical cyclone. Tropical-storm-force winds extend 
outward up to 45 miles (75 km) from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 999 mb (29.50 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?key_messages.
 
RAINFALL: Through early Saturday, Simon is expected to produce
rainfall totals of 1 to 2 inches with isolated maximum amounts of 3
inches over portions of the state of Baja California Sur.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Simon could affect portions of the coast 
of west-central Mexico and Baja California Sur during the next day 
or so. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and 
rip current conditions. Please consult products from your local 
weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Papin

item.description:

Tropical Storm Simon Discussion Number  33
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
800 AM MST Thu Oct 15 2026
 
First light visible imagery, along with GPM and AMSR-3 microwave
data, show that the convective organization of Simon has changed a
bit, with the main convection now in a band to the west of the
center. The various subjective and objective satellite intensity
estimates are in the 40-55 kt range and have not changed much
during the past 6 h. Based on this, the initial intensity remains a
possibly generous 50 kt.
 
The microwave overpasses suggest the center of Simon is a little to
the east of the previous advisory position, and it appears that the
cyclone may be making a small loop in its track. Little motion is
expected for the next 12 h or so as Simon remains embedded in an
area of weak steering currents. After that time, a mid- to
upper-level low is forecast to form near or west of the northern
Baja California Peninsula while a weak mid-level ridge develops over
northern and central Mexico. This should cause Simon to move
northwestward near, but west of, the coast of Baja California Sur,
and this motion is expected to continue until the system
dissipates. The current track guidance is in better agreement in
both direction and speed that it was 24 h ago, and the new forecast
track lies near the center of the guidance envelope. The new
forecast is a little to the east of the previous forecast through
60 h based mainly on the initial position, and after that it is
close to the previous forecast. Given the new track forecast and
the small size of Simon, wind watches are not needed for Baja
California Sur at this time.
 
The shear over Simon has decreased since yesterday, and it should
remain light for the next 12-18 h. However, the storm is embedded
is a dry air mass, so it likely will not be able to take advantage
of the decreased shear. After 18 h, southerly and southwesterly
upper-level winds are forecast to increase between the trough to the
northwest of Simon and Hurricane Trudy to the southeast. This will
result in strong shear over Simon that should cause the cyclone to
weaken. The intensity forecast shows the system becoming a remnant
low pressure area by 72 h and dissipating completely by 120 h, and
global model guidance suggests these events could happen earlier
than currently forecast.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Interests in Baja California Sur should continue to closely
monitor the latest updates as Simon is expected to pass near or west
of that area this weekend.
 
2. Large swells will likely affect portions of the coast of
west-central Mexico and Baja California Sur over the next couple of
days. These swells could cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions.
